Senior QA Specialist, Denmark / Quality Assurance

• Location: Denmark – working across our manufacturing sites in Assens, Holstebro and Svendborg

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: On-site at our manufacturing sites

• Contract type / duration: Permanent

• Travel: Regular travel between the Assens, Holstebro and Svendborg sites

Are you a hands-on Quality professional who enjoys being close to manufacturing? Do you want to drive a risk-based, data-driven approach to quality across several production sites? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Senior QA Specialist, you will be part of our QA Enable team and play an important role in providing independent quality oversight across our Danish manufacturing sites, covering fine-cut tobacco, pipe tobacco and nicotine pouches. You will work closely with Manufacturing, Supply Chain and other stakeholders to continuously improve our Quality Assurance System and build quality capability on the shop floor. Reporting to the QEHS Manager Mass Market, you will combine hands-on manufacturing support with quality engineering, structured problem solving and continuous improvement. This is a great opportunity to shape how quality is managed across multiple sites in an international organization.

What your day will look like

In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Ensure effective implementation and continuous improvement of the Quality Assurance System at our sites, including Quality Control Plans based on product and process risk and Critical-to-Quality characteristics.

• Provide independent quality insight and challenge to ensure products, materials and processes meet specifications and quality requirements, including Food Safety regulations.

• Enable Manufacturing teams to carry out effective Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), and build their quality capability through coaching in RCA, CAPA, PDCA and other improvement tools.

• Monitor process capability, product conformity, quality KPIs and poor-quality costs through trend analysis and statistical methods, and turn findings into improvements across incoming materials, processes and finished products.

• Support new product introductions and process changes, ensuring quality requirements, risk assessments and controls are in place before implementation, and represent Quality in new product and change-management forums.

• Perform Quality System and process audits, support third-party audits, and keep a strong shop-floor presence to identify emerging quality risks early.

What you'll bring

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Quality, Engineering, Food Science, Chemistry, Process Technology or a related technical or scientific field, or equivalent relevant experience.

• 5+ years of experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering or manufacturing quality, with practical experience of Quality Management Systems, specifications, control plans, deviations/non-conformances, CAPA and internal audits.

• Strong practical knowledge of structured problem-solving methods such as RCA, 5 Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa and PDCA, and the ability to analyse quality and manufacturing data and turn trends into actions.

• A credible, pragmatic and solution-oriented approach - you challenge constructively, stay independent on critical quality decisions and coach teams to take ownership of quality across multiple sites.

• Fluency in Danish and professional working proficiency in English.

• It is an advantage if you have experience from tobacco, nicotine, food, pharmaceutical, chemical, FMCG or another regulated manufacturing environment, knowledge of FMEA, SPC and process capability, advanced Excel or statistical software skills, and experience supporting third-party audits.

Working at STG & What to expect

At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next. At STG you'll find more than a role - you'll find opportunities to grow, collaborate across borders, and make a meaningful impact.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Ready to be part of something bigger? Apply now and discover much more.

Our recruitment process

Before starting our hiring process, your application will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

• Recruiter screen

• Interview with the hiring team

• Assessment, case study, or work sample, if relevant

• Final interview with leadership or key stakeholders

Scandinavian Tobacco Group is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Please be informed that this Direct Search is conducted exclusively by Scandinavian Tobacco Group. We do not accept applications from agencies, and we will not provide compensation for unsolicited CVs.

About the Role

We're seeking a driven Business Intelligence Analyst to join our FP&A team, reporting to our FP&A Data Lead - someone early in their data career who's eager to help build our new data platform and grow with it, in a high-impact role that offers real visibility and room to grow.

Now a delisted, growth-equity backed business, OrderYOYO is entering an exciting new chapter – a clear testament to our bold growth ambitions and the fast paced, high-impact environment we are building.

We're building a new data platform that brings together data from every restaurant partner, both on our own platform and on the platforms we acquire. Our Data team builds the pipelines, warehouse and core models; this role sits between them and the people who use the data, turning what lands in the warehouse into something the business can actually work with.

In this role, you'll gain broad exposure across the business by collaborating with Management, Finance, Commercial teams, Tech and Product Owners. You'll play a key role in turning data into actionable insights, including translating business questions into something measurable, modelling the right data, building the reporting and presenting findings for key stakeholders. As you grow, you'll have the freedom to shape your path based on your strengths and interests.

Here's a taste of what you'll be doing:

• Get to know our data warehouse in depth - what data we have, where it comes from and what it can be trusted for - and help scope and integrate data from the companies we acquire.

• Model data into analysis-ready datasets, so the rest of the FP&A team can find and use the right data without starting from raw data every time.

• Write SQL to pull and shape data for Management, Finance, Commercial and Data Science.

• Build and maintain reporting in Power BI - dashboards, recurring management reports and KPI scorecards - and keep the metric definitions behind them consistent, so the business has one version of each number.

• Check data quality, reconcile figures that don't match across sources, and explain why a number moved.

• Turn stakeholder questions into measurable analysis, such as why a new market is ramping up slower than expected or which partners are at risk of churning, and turn recurring requests into reusable models or reports.

What We Are Looking For In You:

• A degree in a quantitative or data-related field, such as economics, statistics, engineering, computer science or information systems.

• Solid SQL skills you have used in practice - in a job, a project or your studies.

• Some understanding of data modelling (how tables, keys and dimensions fit together), or a clear wish to learn it.

• Experience with, or a strong interest in, a BI tool such as Power BI, Tableau or Looker.

• Strong business sense. Curious about which numbers matter and why the business wants them.

• Structured and careful. You check your own numbers before someone else has to.

• A team player who enjoys helping colleagues get to the data they need, with strong communication in English (Danish is a plus but not a requirement).

Why Join Us?

• Help build a modern data platform early in your career, while it is still taking shape, with data that Management uses to make decisions from day one.

• A clear growth path - from learning the platform and supporting the team, to owning metric definitions and how we report.

• Work in a supportive, team-first culture where we help each other succeed.

• Expect personal development plans and ongoing training tailored to your growth.

• Be part of a high-growth journey in a growth equity-backed company, where ambition meets opportunity - and your impact truly matters.

Great to Have (But Not Required)

• Understanding of database structures and data modelling, such as star schemas and semantic models.

• Understanding of how SQL is used to query, model and transform data.

• Hands-on experience with Power BI, including DAX and Power Query.

• Familiarity with finance or commercial concepts, such as cohort modelling.

What we do at OrderYOYO

OrderYOYO is a provider of white-label online ordering, payment, marketing, and POS software solutions to independent local takeaway restaurants. We are ensuring that small to medium-sized restaurants and chains are not subjected to lofty commissions and giving the restaurant the ownership of their success.

Who we are at OrderYOYO

Company culture is at the forefront of our minds creating an enjoyable, safe working environment where employee personal expression is supported. We are one team here at OrderYOYO and strive to help others succeed. Personal development and training plans are a key part of your journey within OrderYOYO, helping you be the best you can be by providing consistent and ongoing training for all aspects of the business. Our values (Passion, Action, Compassion, One team) are what makes us who we are and will be embedded in your day-to-day no matter what area of the business you work in.

**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are curious, collaborative, customer-minded, and motivated by solving real problems for financial professionals, say hello to SimCorp.

At SimCorp, we are guided by our values: caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. We are a people-centered organization that invests in skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in creating an environment where people can grow, feel heard, and be empowered to make an impact.

If this sounds like you, keep reading.

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**You will join SimCorp’s Product Division and work on one of our most critical front-office capabilities: Portfolio Management.

Portfolio managers at asset management firms operate under increasing pressure: volatile markets, complex portfolios, tighter risk constraints, and the need to make better investment decisions faster. Static reports and disconnected tools are no longer enough. Portfolio managers need software that helps them understand portfolio positioning, risk usage, exposures, scenarios, and investment intent — and then translate that insight into action.

That is what we are building.

Built on the SimCorp One platform, our modern Portfolio Management solution helps portfolio managers monitor portfolios, analyze exposures and risk, evaluate alternatives, rebalance, and act within coherent, workflow-driven software designed for true front-office use.

This role exists because Portfolio Management is a strategic growth area for SimCorp and our clients. As Product Manager / Product Owner, you will help turn real portfolio manager workflows into intuitive, scalable software. You do not need to come from a traditional product-management background to succeed. You may have gained relevant experience through value advisory, pre-sales, consulting, implementation, client advisory, or another role where you worked closely with investment-management clients and translated their needs into practical solutions.

The common thread is this: you understand client problems, can structure them clearly, and are motivated to shape software that helps portfolio managers work better every day.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**As Product Manager, you will be accountable for execution, learning, and impact — not just producing backlog items.

You will:

• 
Own the product direction and backlog for one or more Portfolio Management capabilities.

• 
Translate portfolio manager needs, client feedback, and market insight into clear, actionable product increments.

• 
Lead and continuously prioritize the backlog for one or more full-stack scrum teams, balancing client value, product quality, platform direction, and technical health.

• 
Work closely with engineers, designers, architects, product peers, and client-facing colleagues to shape workflows, interactions, and data models that make sense in real front-office contexts.

• 
Build a strong understanding of portfolio manager workflows, including:

• 
Portfolio monitoring and decision preparation

• 
Exposure and risk analysis

• 
Scenario evaluation and rebalancing

• 
Order generation and execution workflows

• 
Write clear product briefs, user stories, acceptance criteria, and decision material focused on user intent and business outcomes.

• 
Use client feedback, internal expertise, usage insight, and delivery learning to validate priorities and iterate quickly.

• 
Collaborate with other Product Owners and Product Managers to ensure coherent front-office workflows across Portfolio Management and adjacent product areas.

• 
Support demos, discovery conversations, and client discussions by grounding the conversation in real portfolio manager use cases.

• 
Act as a consistent voice of the portfolio manager in product, design, and delivery decisions.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with strong ownership, visibility, and direct impact.

**What We Value

**Most importantly, you can see yourself thriving in the role described above. How you acquired the skills matters less than how you apply them.

You may be a strong fit if you have several of the following:

• Experience working with asset managers, investment teams, front-office users, or investment-management technology.

• A background in one or more of the following areas:

• Product management or product ownership

• Value advisory or solution advisory

• Pre-sales or solution consulting

• Business consulting or implementation consulting

• Client advisory, customer success, or professional services in financial technology

• Ability to understand complex client workflows and translate them into clear product needs, priorities, and delivery outcomes.

• Familiarity with portfolio management, portfolio construction, rebalancing, exposure/risk analysis, or order-generation workflows.

• Comfort working with analytics, data, and financial concepts.

• Some knowledge of SimCorp Dimension is clearly a plus, especially if you have worked with front-office, portfolio management, or investment workflows.

Ways of working

• Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

• Ability to structure ambiguous problems and turn them into practical next steps.

• Curiosity about users, workflows, and the “why” behind product decisions.

• Pragmatic, outcome-oriented mindset.

• Ability to zoom out to understand portfolio manager goals — and zoom in to refine workflows, interactions, and details.

• Confidence working with engineers, designers, product peers, and client-facing colleagues.

• Willingness to learn product-management practices if your background is advisory, consulting, or pre-sales.

As a person, you:

• Collaborate naturally with colleagues across disciplines.

• Are comfortable questioning assumptions and navigating complexity.

• Communicate clearly and speak up when needed.

• Balance structure with creativity.

• Care deeply about usability — not just functional completeness.

• Are motivated by creating software that solves real client problems.

**Benefits

**Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. At SimCorp, we believe we can offer more.

In addition to traditional benefits, we provide excellent work-life balance, flexible working hours, and a hybrid workplace model. We also have innovation and personal-development sprints, giving you dedicated time each quarter to master your skills and contribute to company development. There is never only one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible. We process incoming applications continuously. Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.

At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in recruitment. To support fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photos, age, or other non-professional information from your application. Thank you for helping us mitigate bias in the recruitment process.

If you are interested in being part of SimCorp but are not sure whether this role is suitable, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may bring relevant skills from product, advisory, pre-sales, consulting, implementation, or client-facing financial-technology roles. Our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help assess whether this is the right opportunity for you.

We are continually improving our talent-acq

uisition process and aim to make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. During the process, we may ask you to provide feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become a leading provider of integrated investment-management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of Deutsche Börse Group. Following the merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full front-to-back offering for our clients.

We are seeking a Financial Controller to own the integrity of Tekla’s financial reporting across the group. The role combines technical control work, balance sheet reconciliations, consolidation and eliminations, with ownership of a growing set of tax and trade compliance obligations spanning packaging tax, EU and global VAT and customs duties.

The Financial Controller is responsible both for meeting these obligations accurately and on time, and for building the processes, controls and automation that make them repeatable as the business scales. The role sits within an AI-first function focused on operational excellence, so we are looking for someone with a strong digital mindset and a proactive approach to using AI and automation tools to enhance reporting and improve efficiency.

This is a hands-on role, instrumental in ensuring financial accuracy and supporting Tekla's profitability and growth objectives. Reporting to the Finance Director and working closely with the Accounting Manager, the Financial Controller will also contribute to a range of ad hoc financial projects and initiatives across the function.

This is a full-time position based in our open-plan, curated office in Copenhagen.

Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Financial Controlling & Reporting

• Design, implement and manage the group's balance sheet reconciliations, including building standardised templates and processes across multiple entities

• Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and consolidated reporting packs

• Ensure the general ledger is supported by complete, reviewed and documented reconciliations in every period. While taking a hands-on approach to booking journals and ad hoc analysis

Tax & Trade Compliance

• Own end-to-end packaging tax obligations, including data capture, calculation and filing

• Perform compliance reviews over packaging tax, taking a proactive approach as Tekla's global footprint grows

• Analyse customs and import duties, covering tariff classification, country of origin, preferential rates and duty paid versus duty due, and identify recovery and savings opportunities.

Financial Analysis & Performance

• Monitor cash flow, working capital, and financial performance metrics

• Perform variance and accuracy analyses to validate forecasts, budgets, and data integrity, encouraging transparency and accountability

• Investigate material variances and implement process improvements that enhance forecasting precision and analytical rigour

• Provide insightful financial analysis to support business planning, cost efficiencies and strategic priorities

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support business objectives

Process Improvement & Automation

• Drive continuous improvement by leveraging AI and emerging technologies to enhance financial processes, systems, and reporting tools

• Support the automation programme within the accounting team, including Intrastat and VAT reporting

• Review and implement continual improvements in Business Central, including VAT code configuration, VAT statements and financial reports

• Strengthen documentation and controls across all owned processes so they are auditable and transferable

We'd love to hear from you if you are / have:

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field

• Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting standards and tax regulations

• Demonstrable experience of group consolidation and intercompany eliminations in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment

• Strong working knowledge of global VAT and sales tax concepts

• Exposure to packaging tax regimes is an advantage

• Experience designing and operating a balance sheet reconciliation control framework

• Confident ERP user, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

• Demonstrable experience using AI tools such as Claude to optimise and automate financial processes and reporting, for example building reporting dashboards, automating reconciliation and compliance workflows, or analysing large transactional data sets

• Advanced Excel skills and comfort working with large transactional data sets

• Experience from a high-growth business within fashion, textiles or luxury consumer goods is an advantage

• An entrepreneurial mindset with strong interpersonal skills

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

Applications will be reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis, with the aim of the successful candidate joining us as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: PhD in modelling and experiments on PEM electrolysis
jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from January 1st or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks    
The position is offered in relation to the research group "Hydrogen and Electro Fuels" and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Thermal Engineering”.

Your competencies 
As a PhD student in modelling and experiments on PEM water electrolysis, you will work at the intersection of chemical and electrochemical reactor engineering, with a particular emphasis on electrolysis. The project focuses on testing proton exchange membrane electrolysis cells, characterising their electrochemical performance and developing detailed electrochemical cell models. You will design and carry out experiments on single cells, analyse electrochemical behaviour under different operating conditions and use the resulting data to build, calibrate and validate mechanistic models that describe transport, kinetics and degradation phenomena.

An important part of your work will be to investigate how PEM electrolysers perform when conventional materials are partially replaced by recycled ionomers and iridium. You will compare performance, stability and degradation patterns with and without recycled components and translate your findings into a deeper understanding of the underlying electrochemical mechanisms. In parallel, you will conduct techno‑economic assessments of PEM electrolysis systems, including related life cycle assessment studies, to evaluate how material choices, operating strategies and system design affect costs and environmental impacts over the full life cycle.

The PhD project is carried out in the context of the CYCLOPEM, EDSOES and CAPEX projects, which provide access to state‑of‑the‑art experimental facilities and collaboration with academic and industrial partners. You are expected to participate in project meetings and to present your results at international conferences and workshops. In addition, you will contribute to teaching activities within courses on chemical and electrochemical reactors and take part in the daily activities of the Hydrogen and Electro Fuels research group  at AAU Energy, including group meetings, seminars and joint publications.

The applicant must have a relevant professional and/or educational background within thermal, chemical and electrochemical engineering. Modelling of chemical and electrochemical reactor and LCA.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean
and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real‑world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg/Esbjerg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday life. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters.

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Project description (4-5 pages), that: describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. This includes a brief state-of-the-art (including short list of references), a time schedule and how the applicant intends to shed light on the project objectives
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.description:
Changes to this advert made on 13 November 2026:

  The heading of the position has been updated so it correspond correctly to the project and position.

  Two sections has been added:

  Mobility rule and Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)

  Under the section “The position” the acronym and number of the grant has been added (highlighted).

  And due to the changes the application deadline are extended with two weeks from the original application date on 22 November 2026. New deadline for applying is 6 December 2026.

  The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position
 This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (REGULAIRE - Project 101312218) bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

  Project description
 The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

  Description of the scientific environment
 The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.

  The PhD programme
 You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

  Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.   Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is December 6 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in January.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Irina Shklovski by email: ias@di.ku.dk.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**Middle Office Products is part of Wealth Technology, the IT organization behind Nykredit Wealth & Asset Management. We support its three businesses: Nykredit Portefølje Administration (NPA), Nykredit Asset Management (NAM) and Sparinvest.

We build and maintain solutions for controlling, compliance, risk, performance and reporting, and we own the reporting data foundation for Nykredit Wealth & Asset Management. Much of that data starts in SimCorp Dimension, our core portfolio management system, and moves through the data flows and integrations we build around it. We treat data as a product, and the whole team is responsible for keeping it correct and on time.

A large part of our business-critical work currently runs on Wealth DWH, our data warehouse built on SQL Server, SSIS and stored procedures, with its data modelled in Data Vault. Alongside it, we are building Wealth Data Hub, our new data solution in Microsoft Fabric. Both exist to give the business trusted data products for its daily work.

Data moves through Bronze, Silver and Gold layers in OneLake, is built with dbt and orchestrated through Airflow. We manage code and CI/CD in GitHub, infrastructure in Terraform and monitoring in Grafana.

You will work with both Wealth DWH and Wealth Data Hub, allowing you to understand how our existing solutions were built and how our new approach differs. Along the way, you will learn tools used across the industry, applied to financial services.

You will also become part of the Nykredit Group, where we offer opportunities and development to those who are motivated to learn and contribute. Through our student network, Nykredit Youth, you will be invited to professional talks and social events, giving you the opportunity to connect with other students and young professionals across the Group.

**Are you motivated by data engineering and solving problems with code?

**Then you may be the Student Data Engineer we are looking for. In this role, you will:

• Develop and maintain Wealth Data Hub, from dbt models to Airflow pipelines.

• Help keep Wealth DWH and Wealth Data Hub running day to day, including investigating data quality issues.

• Work on reporting used internally, by customers and by regulators.

• Work with SimCorp Dimension and bring its data into Wealth Data Hub.

• Improve monitoring and automation.

• Explore how AI can help us modernise legacy code, automate operations and improve data quality.

As a student assistant, you will work between 10 and 15 hours per week.

**Are you the person we are looking for?

**We imagine that you:

• Are studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Economics or a related field.

• Have some experience with Python and SQL through coursework, projects or a student job, and enjoy solving problems with code.

• Take ownership of your tasks and ask for help when needed.

• Question existing practices and bring new ideas.

• Share what you learn and help make the team better.

• Are curious about AI and interested in understanding where it can create value, and where solid engineering and human judgement matter more.

You do not need prior experience with all the technologies we use. In this role, you will have the opportunity to learn:

• How to work in a terminal and use Git, if you do not already have experience with it

• The technologies behind Wealth Data Hub, including dbt, Airflow and Microsoft Fabric

• How SimCorp Dimension, wealth management and financial reporting work in practice

Don't tick every box? We still encourage you to apply.

**Your new team

**You will join Middle Office Products at our new headquarters in Nordhavn, Copenhagen, and work with data engineers, software engineers, SimCorp Dimension business analysts, a solution architect and a product owner. We work in English, review each other’s code and share what we learn. Your colleagues will support you in your daily work and help you develop your skills.

We look forward to welcoming you as our new colleague.

**Would you like to know more?

**You are welcome to contact me, Head of Wealth Middle Office & Data Technology, Miguel Luis Martinez Picazo on tel. 60 61 06 19 if you have any questions about the position.

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact our recruitment team at nytjob@nykredit.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application, CV (in English) and transcript no later than 29 November 2026.

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

**About Pandektes

**Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

**What We Value

**“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

**Knowing when it’s good enough

**We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

**Knowing when to slow down

**Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

**Make time to experiment

**We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

**The Experience You’ll Bring

**You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

**What we offer

**You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

**Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

**_We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

jobs.occupation: Join our SAP Technology Team at Deloitte Transformation & Technology
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 8,000 employees, Deloitte is one of the largest professional services firms across the Nordics. We help clients navigate complex business and technology transformations by combining deep industry expertise with leading capabilities in Audit, Tax, Advisory, and Consulting.

About the team

Imagine being part of a 140+ strong team that’s reshaping the future of the Nordics’ most exciting companies. We are one of the leading SAP management consultancies in the region, and we are looking for ambitious technology-focused graduates to join our SAP Technology and Transformation team. Our strength lies in our diversity—we come from all educational and personal backgrounds, who always strive to bring the best out in each other.

Who are we in SAP Technology, and what will your tasks be?

As part of our SAP Technology team, you will begin your full-time career in March 2027 and build practical consulting and technical experience from day one. We advise, implement and operate business-driven SAP S/4HANA transformations for some of the largest and most exciting organisations in the Nordics across both the public and private sectors. Depending on your interests and project needs, your work may include analysing technical requirements, supporting solution design, working with data and integrations, contributing to development and testing, and helping clients translate business needs into scalable technology solutions.

Whether your interests lie in SAP architecture, cloud, integrations, development, data and analytics, automation or emerging technologies, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in a client-facing environment.

Job Description

Your Journey from March to the Graduate Programme

You will join us on 1 March 2027, with the option to start either part-time or full-time. During your first months, you will become part of the SAP Technology team, contribute to internal and client-facing work, and build a strong foundation in SAP, consulting and delivery. From August 2027, you will transition to full-time and join the next Nordic SAP Graduate Programme, continuing your development through a structured mix of on-site learning, self-study and on-the-job training.

You will be paired with a buddy and a mentor for continuous guidance and support, while building a powerful network of colleagues across the Nordics.

The journey includes:

Deloitte Technology & Transformation Denmark Consultant Academy:

• Kick things off by mastering the essential consulting toolkit at our Technology & Transformation Academy in Denmark based on an 18 months program. You’ll learn the Deloitte way of collaborative problem-solving.

SAP Bootcamps:

• You will receive an introduction to SAP S/4HANA alongside other graduates from across the Nordics. You will participate in two bootcamps held at various locations in Europe, offering a comprehensive overview of SAP’s functional areas. The bootcamps culminate with deep-dive training sessions combining your newly acquired theoretical knowledge with practical, hands-on exercises in SAP S/4HANA.

Live Project Experience:

• This is where the magic happens. You’ll join a project team and put your new skills to the test on a real client engagement, experiencing firsthand what it means to be a consultant.

SAP Certifications:

• As an SAP consultant, you will engage in self-study during your graduate program to prepare for and pass one or more SAP certifications that are relevant within your area of work.

Overall, you will contribute to client engagements from March while building the experience needed to get the most from the Nordic SAP Graduate Programme beginning in August 2027.

You will help clients transform their technology landscapes with SAP S/4HANA and develop towards a career as an SAP technology consultant.

Qualifications

What you bring to the team:

• You have a high level of written and oral proficiency in English and Danish.

• You are ambitious, curious and eager to learn, with a clear interest in technology and how it can solve business challenges.

• You can communicate technical topics clearly and confidently to both technical and non-technical colleagues and clients.

• You are a team player and have experience collaborating with others, for example through a student job, internship or university project.

• You have completed, or will complete before 1 March 2027, a relevant master’s degree or other formal education within areas such as computer science, software engineering, information technology, data science, business analytics, engineering or a related field.

• You are a natural problem-solver who can break down complex technical challenges into clear, actionable solutions.

• The position is in our Copenhagen office – the right to live and work in Denmark is required.

• You are willing to travel, as we work in a hybrid setup for many of our clients in the Nordics and Europe.

It is a bonus if you also have:

• An understanding of ERP systems and/or SAP.

• Experience with one or more programming or scripting languages, such as Java, JavaScript, Python, SQL or ABAP.

• Familiarity with databases, APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, software development, data engineering or analytics.

• Experience from a student job, internship, thesis or project where you applied technology to a practical problem.

What we offer

• You will get the opportunity to work with and learn from some of the best and brightest minds in the technology and consulting space.

• You will be a part of a dynamic, ambitious, and fun group of people who always put each other first, and have a strong focus on well-being, inclusion, and community.

We place a strong emphasis on feedback and provide opportunities to build a solid foundation for both professional and personal development.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Tell us where you see yourself making the greatest impact within SAP Technology.

We are particularly interested in candidates motivated by one or more of the following areas:

• SAP architecture and cloud

• Application development and automation

• Data, analytics and data engineering

• Integrations and APIs

• Technical delivery, testing and operations

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, and grade transcript by 01.01.2027. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: 01.03.2027

Please do not hesitate to call Johanna Kofoed Quinn, Consultant at +45 31 55 43 33, if you have any questions about the position.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

**Your new team

Working closely with commercial, trading, marketing, product, technology, and analytics stakeholders, you will help shape the future of eCommerce analytics at Pandora and ensure insights play a central role in how we grow and evolve our digital business.

**Additional Information

**

**Did we get your attention?

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position on statistical genetics in plant breeding with special focus on cultivar mixtures in wheat
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position
The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The position provides excellent possibilities for access to state-of-the-art tools for simulation and for the analysis of complex genomic datasets, writing publications, and collaboration with industry partners as well as with other national and international research groups.

Qualifications
• Ph.D. or equivalent in plant/animal breeding, quantitative genetics, quantitative genomics, statistics, or related fields.
• Strong interest in use of stochastic models for the analysis of phenotypic and genomic data.
• Dedicated to developed statistical models in modern plant breeding
• Good understanding of methods used in genomic prediction.
• General understanding of commercial breeding programs.
• Inspiration and experience from working in a commercial breeding program will be valuable.
• Good ability to conduct large-scale computations.
• Documented skills in writing and publishing papers of the highest international standard.
• Good skills in oral and written communication in English.
• Ability to work in a large and diverse group of researchers and collaborate with national and international partners from research and industry.
Who we are:
Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG)
The institute like center, QGG, is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics () at Aarhus University. We perform basic and applied research within livestock and plant breeding as well as human applications in precision medicine. The research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development, basic analysis, and application of the developed methods on practical problems across species in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research Center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strive for an excellent working environment. We therefore value self-leadership, open communication, respect for diversity and success in mentoring, supervision and teaching. The main work location will be the main campus close to Aarhus city center.

Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Research Center Flakkebjerg, Forsøgsvej 1, 4200 Slagelse, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact Information
If you have any questions about the positions, please contact Associate Professor Bjarne Nielsen, +45 4140 9040, e-mail: Bjarne@qgg.au.dk.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

About Chr. Olesen Group

Chr. Olesen Group is a leading international distribution company specializing in vitamins, minerals, and active pharmaceutical ingredients for the feed, food, pharma, and technical industries. With products sourced primarily from Asia, we proudly serve esteemed customers worldwide. As a family-owned business led by the 4th and 5th generations, we combine significant turnover with a close-knit team, making our roles both challenging and rewarding. Discover more about our fascinating history at www.chr-olesen.dk.

About the Role

Key Skills for Success

• Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial processes, and internal controls, with the ability to translate Group standards and procedures into consistent day-to-day practices.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Business Central.

• Ability to take ownership, work independently, and manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

• A proactive and pragmatic approach, with the flexibility to handle both recurring responsibilities and a broad range of ad hoc assignments.

• Experience in Microsoft Excel and Power BI.

• Fluency in English, both written and spoken.

Why Chr. Olesen Group?

• Global Exposure: Work with a diverse team across multiple countries and gain invaluable international experience.

• Career Growth: We believe in nurturing talent and providing opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

• Innovative Environment: Be part of a forward-thinking company that leverages cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions.

Are You Our New Colleague?

If you are a proactive and analytical finance professional who enjoys taking ownership, working internationally, and being close to the business, we would love to hear from you. Submit your application here.

10. December 2026

_**About The Job

**We believe access to global capital markets is not only for the privileged few. Our vision is to enable people to fulfil their financial aspirations to make an impact. That is why we use the power of technology to deliver clients what they need, when they need it in a user-friendly and personalized experience.
